chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Bashar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'In how much did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) set the zakat?' He said: 'In every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams. But if it falls short, there is no zakat on it. And regarding gold, in every twenty dinars, half a dinar. But if it falls short, there is no zakat on it.'

key_terms.الدرهم: Dirham — a silver coin used as currency in early Islamic economies
key_terms.الدينار: Dinar — a gold coin used as currency in early Islamic economies
key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.نصاب: Nisab — the minimum threshold of wealth that makes zakat obligatory
key_terms.نقصت: Deficient/falls short — indicates amount below the nisab threshold

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat threshold for silver and gold according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a direct question posed to Imam Abu al-Hasan (AS) about the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on silver and gold as established by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). The Imam confirms the prophetic rulings: zakat on silver is 2.5% (5 dirhams per 200 dirhams), and on gold is 2.5% (half dinar per 20 dinars). The phrase 'if it falls short' (naqasat) indicates that there is no zakat obligation on amounts below the nisab threshold, a key principle in Islamic financial law that protects those of modest means.
